text:
olivia: quick follow-up from the bake — noticed a recurring pattern where eu clusters pick cheaper fp16 pools but latency jumps by ~25ms for tail requests. not catastrophic but enough to break some SLOs.

ravi: spotted the same in trace charts this morning. looks correlated with probe sampling frequency + a cost smoothing step that biases score slightly toward cheaper regions.

sam: can you paste an example route trace? is this during sustained load or bursts?

olivia: here's a trimmed example from the decision log (sensitive fields removed):

```
route_request { tenant: "acme" region_pref: [eu] probes: { eu-west: {score: 0.72,cost: 0.3,probe_ts: 1755550100}, eu-central: {score:0.70,cost:0.45,probe_ts:1755550050}} policy: {latency_weight: 0.6, cost_weight: 0.4, smoothing_window: 60}
chosen: eu-west (cheaper) -> served on g4x -> tail 95p +22ms
```

olivia: note probe_ts for eu-west is fresher; eu-central probe is 1m stale but its measured latency was consistently lower. smoothing + recency wins here.

tara: this feels like our probe recency vs stability tradeoff. if recency gets too much influence we chase noisy short-term measurements.

kai: possible mitigation: decouple cost-driven adjustments from the immediate probe score used for latency-sensitive buckets. basically two scores: short-term probe for freshness (used for capacity decisions) and stable score for SLO routing.

ravi: +1. implementation thought: keep probe raw measurements, and maintain two aggregates: exp_moving_avg (alpha_high) and windowed_median (long). use a simple selector: if request.latency_sensitivity == high -> pick using windowed_median; else use emavg + cost penalty.

sam: sketch of the scoring change i had in mind:

```
// per-region multiply: final_score = latency_score * latency_weight + cost_score * cost_weight
latency_score = (is_latency_sensitive ? stable_latency_agg : emavg_latency)
cost_score = normalize(cost)
apply_penalty_for_stale_probes(latency_score, probe_age)
```

sam: plus we should cap cost_weight for latency-sensitive buckets to something small (eg 0.05) so cost never trumps obvious latency regressions.

olivia: operationally we need a fallback: if stable_agg is missing (new region/model) fall back to emavg but mark traffic as canary and route a % to stable candidates once enough samples collected.

tara: we should also add an observability change: expose chosen_score_components in the routing trace so SRE and customers can see "why" a region was chosen (cost vs latency vs recency).

kai: agree. and add an autotune job that runs offline sims with traffic traces to suggest cost_weight per-tenant class. avoids hardcoding one global value.

ravi: question on data plane changes — does this require a hotreload of policy kernels? or can we implement as a lightweight pre-routing transform?

sam: prefer pre-routing transform on the sidecar/decision-layer so we don't touch the core runtime. keep kernel change minimal: new fields in route decision proto (score_components, chosen_agg_type).

olivia: ops checklist for the change:
- add stable_agg compute in probe service (backfill historical windows)
- add pre-routing selector logic in policy adapter (feature flagged)
- emit diagnostics (score breakdown + probe ages)
- rollout in canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback guard on 95p latency

tara: +1 on rollout plan. also let's add a safety throttle: if tail latency increases by >10% for two consecutive minutes, force fallback to previous selection path.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://redwood.internal/ops/1234 (canary flags: route_score_separation) :white_check_mark:

ravi: one more thought: we should avoid a hard boundary for "latency_sensitive" — instead derive sensitivity from route config (max_allowed_p95) so the system is expressive per-route.

sam: good call. will update the proto with optional max_p95_hint and make cost_weight computed from (max_allowed_p95) with sensible caps.

olivia: ok next steps: sam to PR scoring change + proto, kai to prototype stable_agg offline job, ravi/tara to update rollout/playbook. i'll coordinate canary windows with SRE.

sam: I'll aim for a draft PR today. keeping it feature-flagged and unit tested.

tara: thanks all. feel free to ping me if you want a quick review of the observability UI bits.

olivia: thanks everyone :rocket:

infra-bot: scheduled canary run for 1755551300 -> 1755551900
